provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Original mechanism: every non-background (0) cell is recoloured by the rank of its column among occupied columns, ordered left to right, giving colours 1..4. The factory tracks how the column axis and its left-to-right direction move under the D4 transform: horizontal flip reverses the direction; each clockwise rotation turns column order into row order with the same direction, and row order into column order with reversed direction. The result is (col,asc),(row,asc),(col,desc),(row,desc) for d4=0..3, and (col,desc),(row,desc),(col,asc),(row,asc) for d4=4..7. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. It masks cells that differ from the background constant palette[5]. It ranks the occupied columns or rows in the chosen direction and paints each one palette[rank+1]. Cells that share a line get the same colour even when they belong to different connected shapes, which matches the per-column split seen in the fixtures.
draft_notes.limitations: The background is fixed as palette[5] rather than inferred, which matches the generator's constant background of 5. The constructor always produces exactly four occupied lines; if more than nine ever occurred, extra ranks would reuse the last palette colour. The demonstrations are not used, since the rule is fully determined by the input. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule. No tests were run.
